title: Terryworld

description.main: The 2008 Taschen 25th Anniversary edition of Terryworld, Dian Hanson's survey of Terry Richardson's flash-lit portraits, nudes and fashion work, revised from the 2004 original with over seventy added photographs. Hardcover with pictorial jacket, 288 pages, texts by Gavin McInnes and Olivier Zahm.
description.extended:
Terryworld is the Taschen survey that fixed Terry Richardson's public image, and this is the 2008 25th Anniversary edition, revised and enlarged from the 2004 original.

Dian Hanson edited the book. Its 288 pages hold portraits, nudes, fashion work and studio sex pictures, shot with a point-and-shoot camera against bare white walls, with Richardson in the frame as often as his subjects. Gavin McInnes and Olivier Zahm contribute texts in English, French and German. The title comes from Richardson's 2004 exhibition at Deitch Projects in New York. This printing adds more than seventy photographs and has a new jacket. Richardson reclines shirtless on the front, the T-Bone tattoo on his belly runs up the spine under the Taschen 25 mark, and his legs fill the back.

Richardson, born in New York in 1965, is the son of fashion photographer Bob Richardson. He built this flash-lit snapshot look in the 1990s for Vice, Purple and i-D and carried it into campaigns for Marc Jacobs, Supreme, Tom Ford and Yves Saint Laurent. His other books include Hysteric Glamour, Son of Bob, Kibosh and Mom & Dad. In 2017, after years of misconduct allegations from models, Condé Nast and several fashion houses stopped commissioning him.
description.artist_bio: Terry Richardson (born 1965, New York) is an American fashion photographer, son of Bob Richardson, known for a direct-flash snapshot style used in editorial for Vice, Purple, Rolling Stone, GQ and Vogue and in campaigns for Marc Jacobs, Supreme, Tom Ford and Yves Saint Laurent. In 2017 Condé Nast, Valentino and Bulgari stopped commissioning him following sexual misconduct allegations; he has not actively worked since 2018.
description.exhibition_context: The book shares its title with Richardson's 2004 exhibition at Deitch Projects, New York, which the 2004 first edition accompanied.
